_comment: Homestead's magic. The big temple sends out a priest of its people as soon as it is finished and then every priestSeconds. Small temples turn their people's drink into mana for their player, one unit every templeSeconds (mana per unit below). A people's priests know the eight spells of its menu. A spell is cast at a point up to range fields from the priest (the original's 24; bowmen reach 14) and works within its radius there, if someone or something it works on is there. Priests can be attacked (health).
_costComment: costIncrease: percent each cast of a spell makes the player's next one of the same spell dearer, rounded up (original: 25 – 20, 25, 32, 40 …; wiki.siedler3.net, Mana & Magie); 0 = constant. The settings (military tab) override it for new games.
_castComment: castSeconds: how long the priest stands casting; the spell takes effect at once when it begins.

spells._comment: Values of the original (wiki.siedler3.net, Mana und Magie): cost (initial mana), radius (area around the target; 0: the whole map), count (most units or goods), seconds. Spells on units for a while (Haste, Fear, Strengthen, Shield, CursedArrows, Freeze) also take soldiers of a military building (on top of it, at the door, on the way in); those moving or changing units (Convert, Scatter, Reinforce, BowsToPioneers) only units outside: priests, soldiers, scouts, geologists, pioneers. Recasting renews the time, effects do not add up. placeholder: not made yet (shown, cannot be cast). anywhere: cast at any point of the map without walking there.
spells._summonComment: SummonGoods (heavenly gifts, every people): piles (min, max) piles of amount (min, max) goods appear around the target, each of a random group, then a random material of it; extra: further piles per people, each with its chance.

_ownComment: The people's own spell: the one the AI casts in fights.
_menuComment: The priests' spell menu per people, top to bottom like the original (icons: spellMenu in data/ui.json, order checked against them).
_upgradesComment: Soldier upgrades at a small temple (like the original): first all three soldier types one after the other to level 2 (Feldwebel), only then to level 3 (Hauptmann). Only soldiers trained afterwards get the new level. Mana goes to two accounts: spells spend it, upgrades only ask how much the player has earned in all (they spend nothing). manaEarned: mana earned in all for the player's 1st, 2nd, ... upgrade, whichever type (the original's, wiki.siedler3.net).
